Service Details:
Weekly collection includes:
• 1 gray cart for household trash (bagged and inside the cart)
• 1 blue cart for recycling (loose, clean, and dry items only. No
plastic bags!)
• Up to 10 items (any combination of compostable yard bags,
reusable containers, and up to 4 bundles)
Collection Guidelines
• Set your carts out by 6:00 a.m. on your collection day.
• Collection may occur anytime between 6:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.
• Bring carts back from the curb within 24 hours after collection.
• Each cart, yard waste bag, or bundle must weigh less than 50 lbs.
• Only trash inside the gray county-provided cart will be collected.
No loose trash or piles placed outside the cart will be collected.
• Place carts with lid closed and the wheels of the cart facing
your house, 3 feet away from obstructions including mail boxes,
vehicles, and other carts.
Additional Options for Extra Trash/Recycling:
If you have more trash or recyclables than your regular service
allows, here are your options:
• Request Additional Service
Contact customer service for extra or additional trash
and recycling service or submit your request online:
www.fairfaxcounty.gov/publicworks/recycling-trash/
trashrecycling-container-request
• Self-Haul Excess Materials to the following locations:
» I-95 Landfill Complex (9850 Furnace Rd, Lorton, VA 22079)
» I-66 Transfer Station (4618E West Ox Rd, Fairfax, VA 22030)
Fees:
The annual refuse fee is $630, divided into two equal installments
included in the first and second real estate tax bills. For billing
questions: DTARED@fairfaxcounty.gov or call 703-324-4802.
Unacceptable Materials
Please do NOT place the following items in your trash/recycling carts:
• Liquids, including sewage or septic waste
• Hazardous waste, such as paint, oil, asbestos, chemicals, or
lithium batteries
• Compressed cylinders (any size)
• Automobile parts, including batteries and tires
• Rechargeable batteries of any kind
• Construction and demolition debris, such as drywall, shingles,
roofing materials, insulation, or concrete
• Animal carcasses
• Broken glass, unless boxed, taped shut, and clearly labeled
“GLASS”
• Bio-hazardous medical waste

Yard waste collection makes it easy to manage your outdoor debris.
Here’s what you need to know:
Collection Schedule:
• March 1 through December 24: yard waste (grass, leaves, and
trimmings) is collected separately from trash.
• December 25 through February 28/29: Bag your yard waste
and place it in your trash cart for regular collection.
How to Prepare Yard Waste:
• Use compostable paper bags, rigid containers, or tie yard waste
into bundles:
• Limit yard waste to 10 items (any combination of compostable
bags, containers, and up to 4 bundles).
• Bundles should be no longer than 4 feet, 6 inches in diameter and
weigh less than 50 pounds.
• If you have more than 4 bundles, please schedule a brush special
pickup.
What is NOT Considered Yard Waste:
• Soil, mulch, sod, stumps, whole trees, large branches, and limbs
• Invasive plants or bamboo (Bamboo requires a bulk special
pickup scheduling)
